title: LLM Endpoints — Counterplay Cheatsheet for Field
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick-reference for AE/SDR/SE when positioning Redwood vs other LLM API providers. Not a pitch script — a field cheat sheet with short plays and technical counters.
- Use in discovery, competitive call, and tech deep-dive.

Top-line positioning bites (1-liners):
- For product and infra teams that need predictable inference economics and enterprise controls, Redwood is the inference platform that treats serving as a first-class product — not just model access.
- If a customer cares about consistent latency, cost visibility, and easy rollout between hosted/dedicated/private, lead with predictable SLAs and unified tooling.

Common competitor categories and quick frames:
- Simpler LLM API players (fast onboarding, wide model choice): "Great for prototypes. Redwood is the handoff to production — lower unit costs at scale and stronger operational controls."
- Cloud-managed model endpoints (vendor infra + model hosting): "They give GPUs but you still own the serving logic. Redwood gives a runtime + orchestration and built-in fallback/failover specifically tuned for production LLM workloads."
- Self-hosted inference runtimes (open-source projects): "More control but more ops. Redwood packages the runtime + lifecycle + safety and shifts maintenance off your plate if you want it."

Feature delta cheat matrix (speech-sized bullets for customer-facing calls):
- Latency SLOs: Redwood — SLA-backed targets + regional routing; competitors — often best-effort or infra-dependent.
- Cost controls: Redwood — token-level spend breakdowns + Optimize recommendations; competitors — limited visibility or coarse metrics.
- Deployment modes: Redwood — hosted, dedicated, private (same API); competitors — scattered (hosted OR self-hosted).
- Rollouts & fallbacks: Redwood — canary/A-B/fallback per-route; competitors — manual or limited.
- Observability: Redwood Console — token-level traces, prompt set regressions; competitors — basic logs / metrics.

Customer pain signals that map to Redwood strengths:
- "We get surprise bills or token spikes" -> lead with cost transparency, token-level traces and Optimize toolkit.
- "Our models slow down unpredictably" -> lead with latency SLOs, smart routing, and autoscaled Dedicated pools.
- "We can't ship in regulated environments" -> lead with Private/VPC and on-prem options + KMS/HSM integration.

Rebuttals to typical objections (short, field-ready):
- "I can just use cloud provider endpoints for cheaper pricing."
  - Counter: Cloud GPUs are raw capacity; total cost includes engineering ops and suboptimal batching. Redwood reduces per-token cost by caching/continuous batching and recommends quantization where it keeps quality. Ask: what does your ops time look like for peak events?

- "Open-source runtimes give us the most control — why pay a platform?"
  - Counter: If you want full control and ops bandwidth, great. If you want to move faster without hiring a dedicated infra team, Redwood gives the runtime + tuning + rollouts and can run private. Offer: pilot on Dedicated to validate ops delta.

- "We're worried about model quality drift if you optimize aggressively."
  - Counter: Redwood Optimize hooks quality monitoring to prompt sets and raises regression alerts; rollouts are gradual with automatic fallback to preserve experience.

Demo play snippets (30–90s talking points):
- Cost transparency demo lead: open Console -> show token-level cost waterfall for a route -> call out a single user session and the breakdown -> explain Optimize suggestion that reduced token usage by X% in pilot.
- Reliability demo lead: show routing policy page -> demonstrate automatic fallback config -> simulate a region outage and show request routing to backup model.

Technical traps & escalation checklist for SEs:
- Trap: Customer compares peak throughput without accounting for batching effects.
  - Fix: Ask for request distribution (seq lengths, concurrency). Show how continuous batching changes effective throughput.
- Trap: Opponent claims lower per-token price publicly.
  - Fix: Push for TCO: CPU/GPU allocation inefficiencies, re-run costs, dataset transfer. Offer to model a 3-month forecast with their telemetry.
- Trap: Customer 'security-first' — compares to in-house due to compliance fears.
  - Fix: Map controls: VPC, on-prem package, KMS/HSM, audit logs. Offer architecture review with security PM.

Suggested discovery checklist (questions for AE/SE):
- What is your traffic shape (median & p95 tokens, requests per minute, burstiness)?
- Do you need on-prem or VPC networking for regulated data?
- How do you measure quality regressions today (canary prompts, evals)?
- What SLAs matter most (p99 latency, availability, jitter)?
- What budget model do you prefer (usage, committed reserved)?

Quick one-line closes by persona:
- Engineering lead: "We help reduce ops surface and hand off serving pains while preserving performance controls."
- Product manager: "Ship consistent LLM features faster — one API and rollout model across environments."
- CIO/Security: "We support private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations with audit trails."

- Feed back any new competitive claims to #g2m-llm-battlecards with evidence.
